hypotheses.claim: Persistence/availability itself is the main driver of future adaptive value.
hypotheses.next: No direct reopen; persistence may appear as one input inside other mechanisms.
hypotheses.verdict: Persistent availability is a precondition for later use, not evidence of value. Reconstructable state, unused capabilities and persistent failed priors falsify the dominant form.

hypotheses.claim: Deeper change classes such as method/meta-selection compound more reliably than state/capability changes.
hypotheses.next: Keep change depth as descriptive vocabulary only.
hypotheses.verdict: Depth rank predicts later value poorly; deep meta-priors can be neutral or harmful while shallow procedures can transfer.

hypotheses.claim: Future-model-robust responsibility placement is broadly a causal driver of compounding.
hypotheses.next: Use narrower H-BURDEN-THRESHOLD; do not promote broad H-RESP.
hypotheses.verdict: Responsibility placement strongly explains Agent-first history, but F10A shows future-model robustness/determinism is not sufficient for useful externalization.

hypotheses.claim: A mechanically stable responsibility becomes valuable to externalize when observed reconstruction complexity/frequency exceeds model reliability or recurring cost, provided owner/authority placement remains sound.
hypotheses.next: Reopen only on a natural workload with pre-observed reconstruction burden; never manufacture raw complexity to justify a projection.
hypotheses.verdict: Future-model robustness and correct responsibility placement make externalization safe to own, but do not make it useful. Measured recurring reconstruction complexity/error/cost determines whether a smallest mechanical projection adds value; simple deterministic or reconciliation tasks can already be model-ceiling.

hypotheses.claim: Local observable causal credit is a general driver of transfer.
hypotheses.next: Revisit only with a new balanced prospective task family that independently controls binding, adjacency and prior.
hypotheses.verdict: F3 is the strongest retrospective separator, but F9 fails the prospective admission rule and reveals label-prior/representation confounding.

hypotheses.claim: Explicitly generating more causal variants is the current bottleneck for recursive improvement.
hypotheses.next: Reopen only after natural repeated evidence that a strong direct model fails to generate the correct causal family.
hypotheses.verdict: Across closed-menu F4 and open-ended F8A, explicit multi-candidate generation has no stable final diagnosis or oracle-candidate-coverage advantage and worsens validity/compliance in some settings. Extra candidates can move the bottleneck into selection.

hypotheses.claim: Independent negative feedback/rollback/deletion is causally required to prevent harmful self-reinforcement.
hypotheses.next: Reopen on a natural evaluator-attack/performative loop with independent world truth; do not weaken CEL or inject a toy reward hack merely to make regulation useful.
hypotheses.verdict: Regulation is identifiable only when a candidate can influence its future evaluator/evidence, proxy truth can diverge from independent consequence truth, and an unregulated baseline actually false-reinforces. Current CEL already separates candidate from grader/holdout and no natural false-self-reinforcing Computing loop was found.

hypotheses.claim: Persisted adaptive rules/examples can become model- and task-dependent decision-boundary biases, so retained learning can amplify error as well as value.
evidence: F18 natural Harness P3 -> P1/P2 support shift
hypotheses.next: Seek a second materially different prior/model-task-environment shift with downstream owner-native outcome. No TTL or automatic prior engine is earned.
hypotheses.verdict: Retained priors remain interventions and can become overbroad when their support conditions change. F18 shows a natural Harness shift where expire-all would delete still-valid clauses and keep-all would preserve an overbroad negative; clause-level support-bound revalidation correctly retains, strengthens, or narrows different parts. Age/revision are review triggers, not semantic falsifiers.

hypotheses.claim: When candidate generation is already adequate, recursive improvement may be limited more by selecting/crediting among candidates than by generating more variants.
hypotheses.next: Only test if a natural candidate-rich failure appears; do not invent a selector service.
hypotheses.verdict: Consistent with variation failures but not yet independently manipulated.

hypotheses.claim: Capabilities with low current consumption may still deserve retention because they expand the adjacent possible or preserve future branching value under uncertain workloads.
evidence: HD2-N2 recurrence across HD2–HD6 historical epochs
hypotheses.next: Do not infer a winner before F14 closes. Append only qualifying post-t0 events.
hypotheses.verdict: Latent option value remains real, but prospective retention policy remains unresolved. F14 freezes three t0 shadow policies over 12 real capabilities and delegates the oracle to post-cutoff owner/external demand, measuring realized carrying/reacquisition/blocking regret rather than label prediction.

hypotheses.claim: Adaptive value may be interactional: changes with weak marginal value alone can create large value jointly, invalidating single-change deletion/credit rules.
evidence: F15 current Finance x Workstation reobservation
hypotheses.next: Wait for a naturally non-additive cross-domain workload; do not manufacture arm failure.
hypotheses.verdict: F12 still proves one Harness-local mechanical interaction. F15 refused a natural cross-domain candidate because ambient OKX access already completed the same owner-relevant read-only endpoint; scoped egress was faster but did not uniquely create capability. Broad coalition credit remains unproven.

hypotheses.claim: Recursive adaptation requires a stable identity/invariant boundary that determines what commitments/evidence survive self-change and what must be invalidated.
evidence: F19 Harness old-revision durable Run reopened/resumed by current Harness
hypotheses.next: Replicate on a materially different migration involving schema/representation or owner-boundary change; measure stale-state carryover, evidence interpretability, authority violations, and continuation correctness.
hypotheses.verdict: One real Harness P0->P2 migration rejects byte-sameness, reset-all, and silent inherit-all-installed in favor of invariant-bound continuity: exact Run identity, Contract/authority digests, evidence and health survived implementation change while new P1/P2 installed mechanisms did not silently enter the old Run or resumed turn authority.

hypotheses.claim: The system can reliably discover the next important improvement pressure rather than only improve a given well-formed problem.
hypotheses.next: Continue only on natural events. Need genuine positive-pressure events whose decisive probes change downstream decisions before evaluating certificate benefit.
hypotheses.verdict: C6 remains negative. F17 now has three natural post-t0 owner controls across Computing/Game/Studio: direct full review is valid 6/6 and certificate is valid 5/6; every valid run chooses NO_OP, so false promotion is zero so far. Certificate has no observed semantic benefit on controls and one structured-validity failure. No positive-pressure event has occurred, so comparative pressure-discovery value is unresolved.

hypotheses.claim: A generic low-cost option-aware retention checklist can reliably identify dormant capabilities worth carrying before future workloads are known.
hypotheses.next: Do not tune on F11. Any future policy test must use a precommitted hidden future workload distribution with realized cost/regret.
hypotheses.verdict: F11 OPTION_AWARE has directionally higher holdout valid accuracy but only 2 paired holdout wins / 1 loss / 19 ties and misses the strongest owner-native P2 positive in every valid OPTION run. Both treatments already have 100% valid negative specificity.

hypotheses.claim: A retained prior should be revalidated at the granularity of its causal/support conditions; age/revision/model change creates review pressure but does not by itself invalidate every clause.
hypotheses.next: Require a second independent prior-shift replication before any reusable automation.
hypotheses.verdict: In the natural Harness shift, support-bound revalidation retains still-valid anti-authority clauses while narrowing the now-overbroad claim that capability compilation is wholly unproven.

hypotheses.claim: Across implementation change, durable identity is better preserved by invariant-bound lineage/commitment/evidence/authority continuity than by byte sameness, reset-all, or automatic inheritance of all newly installed mechanisms.
hypotheses.next: Replicate across schema/representation or owner-boundary migration before Core consideration.
hypotheses.verdict: Current Harness reopened and completed a Run written by an older revision with exact Run/Contract/Tool digests unchanged; current installed P1/P2 mechanisms were visible at package level but absent from old Run/turn authority.

promotionBoundary: No v1 hypothesis is automatically Computing Knowledge/Core. Emerging candidates require materially different prospective evidence; open candidates are research questions only.
sourceEvidenceBoundary: F0 through F10A only. Inclusion records current research state; it is not architecture, owner policy or promotion authority.

wave3.boundary: No owner reform. Wave 3 changes Computing research/knowledge only.
notAdmitted: F13 prior expiry/revalidation — no clean independent task family

wave4.boundary: No PAL-specific Core promotion or lower-owner reform. F14/F17 require future reality; do not backfill outcomes.
completedOrDisposed: F18 support-bound prior revalidation scoped positive
F19 invariant-bound identity migration scoped positive
